title: Short Fills to the Sync Day: Auto Refill & Medication Sync Settings
content:
A short fill is a fill of fewer days than a full cycle, dispensed to bring a prescription onto the sync day. Auto Refill & Medication Sync programs set per program whether short fills may be dispensed, the fewest days to the sync day for which one is dispensed, and whether the patient pays a copay prorated by days on it.

| Program | Short fill to the sync day may be dispensed | Fewest days to the sync day for which a short fill is dispensed | Copay prorated by days on a short fill |
|---|---|---|---|
| Kestrel Auto Refill 30-Day | No | 0 | No |
| Kestrel Auto Refill 90-Day | No | 0 | No |
| Kestrel Med Sync Monthly | Yes | 3 | Yes |
| Kestrel Med Sync 90-Day | Yes | 3 | Yes |
| Kestrel Med Sync with Adherence Packaging | Yes | 3 | Yes |
| Kestrel Home Delivery Auto Refill | No | 0 | No |

## Setting notes

- The minimum is a whole number of days to the sync day. Where fewer days than the minimum remain to the sync day, the days are carried to the following sync day rather than dispensed as a short fill.
- The three Med Sync programs (Kestrel Med Sync Monthly, Kestrel Med Sync 90-Day, Kestrel Med Sync with Adherence Packaging) all allow short fills, all set the minimum at 3 days, and all prorate the copay by days.
- The three Auto Refill programs (Kestrel Auto Refill 30-Day, Kestrel Auto Refill 90-Day, Kestrel Home Delivery Auto Refill) do not dispense short fills; their minimum reads 0 and no prorated copay applies.
